WindowsActivationSecurityTests.Activatio.reason: The unchanged WindowsActivationSecurity implementation is now shared by Avalonia and the secure Electron helper. Both original and new actual-process tests inspect real mutex/pipe security: current SID owner, protected DACL, exactly two entries in order (deny NETWORK, allow current SID). The pipe reports the actual Electron parent PID for foreground permission; the helper validates this PID against its real OS parent and binds ownership to both the parent handle and stdin EOF. Chromium second-instance/open-url events cannot bypass the Windows channel. The native inspector also verifies those protected objects created by a running Electron frontend in both presentations; no framework-specific security waiver applies.

DataDirectoryOverrideTests.The_compositi.reason: The original real DI assertion is preserved through BackendApplication: LifecycleSyncService and ILifecycleRepository resolve, the connection factory uses selectedRoot/winnow.db, and CoverCacheOptions uses selectedRoot/covers. The real authenticated plugins-directory route supplies the same selected root to Electron AvalonThemeStore; desktop/fullscreen native cases load authored theme files from selectedRoot/themes and verify the database/cache/theme paths. This replaces the Avalonia-only UserThemeStore type while retaining its actual filesystem behavior. Default-root resolution uses the shared WinnowDataLocation migration/fallback operation, while explicit override identity remains separate for Chromium profile, restart, autostart and shell arguments. Linux/macOS package runtime is deferred to the cross-platform milestone; the shared resolver process operation is executed on Windows.
